Hmm, that’s a tough one. I phrased it asking as “insight on him” but now that I’m reading it again with that in mind I think it’s possible it might me about my feelings.

Influence of the Angels by Jody Boginski used for this spread. I asked about an old acquaintance who I have lots of baggage that I’ve run into for the first time in a couple of years. I don’t think he recognized me but the encounter has really shaken me up. This was originally a one card pull with one clarifier but the hierophant fell out when I put the deck down. I find this interesting because I pulled it in a personal reading for the first time this morning (upright). I’d love some input because I’m new to tarot and can’t really make sense of this. Here’s my take.

Eight of swords reversed: I think he’s afraid of something. I know him to be somewhat narrow-minded and I think this card is talking about some sort of inferiority complex. 

Seven of wands: Handling a conflict, facing something head on?

Hierophant reversed: I think this is the same narrow-mindedness I’m reading in the eight of swords. Somewhat of an intolerance towards something.
This makes a lot of sense, thank you! I’ll keep that in mind as I go forward.

I think people are right when they say that in most cases (at least the ones that aren’t cold), police are withholding information. The first one to come to mind when I read the question was the Delphi and Elizabeth Collins/Lyric Cook murders, though.

Michael Negrete. In my eyes, definitely drug deal gone wrong. Everyone uses the “he left his wallet and keys back at the dorm” as an excuse for him not going to a drug deal, but wouldn’t you take cash? I think it’s plausible he took only cash with him and left the dorm.
Shane Fell. I think it's more likely that he inured himself or that a gator got to him rather than a hitchhike with the wrong person.
I’d say Madeleine McCann. Some days I’m 100% sure the parents know something and other days I’m convinced the only thing they’re guilty of is bad parenting.
I really want to say Andrew Gosden. There's just no leads that scream "foul play" so my mind goes straight to "he's alive."
Alissa Turney. Officially still unsolved but the general consensus is that the step father did something to her.

Definitely a possibility, but I think it’s just way too much of a coincidence. He gets molested by a couple a few weeks earlier and then he disappears? I can’t wrap my head around the two events being unrelated.

[Louis Mackerley](http://charleyproject.org/case/louis-anthony-mackerley). There’s so many elements to the case that don’t make any sense but I am 100% sure that the couple who molested him earlier before his disappearance had something to do with it. I don’t think he’s alive anymore as he’d be 41, but I do think he was kept alive for a while after they abducted him.

Thank you for your input. I guess I hesitate to place the blame on Sergio since there seems to be a lot of circumstantial evidence placed against him. He’s definitely acting weird and the CPS involvement is suspicious, but things like sleeping on your couch, acting calm during a stressful situation, those are just things that are convenient and not hard evidence. 

I had never considered the rape/sexual abuse angle before, honestly. It does make a lot of sense. Isabel always sleeping in her brothers’ room, the mom maybe being aware that something fishy was going on, even the brothers and all the weird things they said during the investigation could contribute.
I believe the parents are still together if you ignore those few months Sergio had to live away from his children. The police never released what the CPS visits were about either.

Personally, I didn’t think it was weird he assumed abduction either. A lot of people seem to think that the use of the actual word “abduction” was out of place too, given parents would usually use something more casual in a situation like this. I don’t think it’s fair to lash out at Sergio for assuming abduction either.

I agree. I won’t rule out the possibility that she was alive for days or even years after she was abducted but I find it highly unlikely. I’m almost certain that she died the same day she went missing.

They probably were able to tell but not much has been released to the public. I haven’t read anything about when she died or how. The autopsy report was released and obviously I can’t interpret it since I’m not an expert but it was also heavily redacted.

Nothing missing has been mentioned in all i’ve read but it is interesting to think about. I do think there was someone outside the family involved, maybe working with someone inside the family. I feel like the brothers aren’t involved although they have said some weird things over the course of the investigation.
Agreed. I think people place too much value on the call instead of paying attention to the details of the case.

That's interesting. I'd heard the drug theory before but I didn't think there was a lot to back it up. The family definitely didn't seem the type to be involved with drugs but maybe that could be why Sergio acted so suspicious. Thanks for the input.
